open_threads.thread: Einarsson v. Canada (ICSID Case No. UNCT/20/6): NAFTA Chapter 11 claim on proprietary seismic data as IP (copyright/trade-secret) investment; Canada's regulatory-disclosure regime challenged; Canada's Art. 1121 waiver-consistency objection (double-dipping) documented as a second Ring 3 mechanism — jurisdictional, not procedural (confirmed by Waste Management I and Detroit International Bridge); merits hearing concluded March 2025, post-hearing proceedings ongoing (testimony Aug 2025), no award as of June 2026 — monitor for award.

Trade-secret / clinical-data gap: No publicly known ISDS case has yet asserted pharmaceutical trade secrets or clinical trial data as the primary covered investment — the Ferguson/Kim framework remains theoretical; 1,463 total ISDS cases in UNCTAD Navigator as of December 31, 2025; approximately 13 historical pharmaceutical ISDS cases total; no pharmaceutical trade-secret or clinical-data case identified in 2025–2026 new registrations. Track any new filing under BITs or CPTPP.

Treaty architecture closure (COMPLETE — monitoring): USMCA/CUSMA lapsed US-Canada ISDS after 30 June 2023; CPTPP pharmaceutical test data exclusivity provisions (TPP Art. 18.50) suspended — no direct ISDS hook for clinical data under either major multilateral framework. UK CPTPP accession (Dec 2024) adds investor pool without restoring suspended provisions. Monitor older bilateral BITs and any new ICSID/UNCITRAL pharmaceutical IP registration; monitor Mexico USMCA Art. 20.48 clinical-data non-implementation for Chapter 31 or Annex 14-D proceedings.

China BIT pharmaceutical data exclusivity — MONITORING (Ring 1 + Ring 2 foundations established): Two regulatory layers now in force (State Council DAL Implementing Regs, Jan 2026; NMPA Implementation Measures, May 15, 2026). June 5, 2026 transitional deadline passed — covered-investment set crystallised (companies that filed by June 5 hold formal data exclusivity entitlements; others definitively waived). USTR 2026 Special 301 Report characterises China's pharmaceutical data conditions as 'unfair and discriminatory' (especially the gap on drugs first approved outside China), adding a Ring 2 dimension. European BIT architecture complete: China-Germany BIT (2003) covers 'trade and business secrets'; China-Switzerland BIT (2009) and China-France BIT (2007) cover 'know-how.' EU-China CAI suspended. Monitor US-China negotiations on drugs-approved-outside-China gap; monitor for any ISDS filings under European BITs.

Ring 3 doctrine — abuse of rights / DOB gap: Jason Yu Song v. China (PCA 2019-39, Jan 2025) reveals natural-person nationality-planning gap in DOB clause architecture. 59th Commission session (June 29–July 10, 2026, New York) opens TOMORROW — four-track agenda: procedural Protocol A/CN.9/1246 (evidence, bifurcation, interim measures, manifest lack of merit, security for costs, TPF disclosure, counterclaims, cost allocation); MIC first-tier and appellate statutes from 54th session; MIIR; Advisory Centre (A/CN.9/1265, A/CN.9/1266). DOB provision (Draft Provision 9, WP.253) NOT in A/CN.9/1246; natural-person gap NOT addressed by any July 2026 Commission document. Ring 3 doctrine architecture unchanged. Monitor session outcome by July 10. Next WG III milestones: Tenth Inter-sessional September 7–9, 2026 (Ninh Binh, Vietnam); 55th session October 12–16 Vienna (tentative).
